data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The search for a minimal 13-input sorting network stalls at 45 comparators because no optimal 39-comparator 12-input network can be extended with the 13th channel using 5 or fewer additional comparators, meaning a 44-comparator network cannot be formed by extending an optimal 12-input prefix.","counterconditions":[{"case":"There exists a 12-input sorting network of 39 comparators that has a structural 'opening' allowing the 13th channel to be merged in exactly 5 comparators.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"A 44-comparator 13-input network exists but does not embed any optimal 39-comparator 12-input sorting network as a contiguous prefix.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"If the first 39 comparators form an optimal 12-input sorting network (since S(12)=39), the remaining 5 comparators must merge the 13th channel into the sorted 12 channels. According to the 0-1 principle, the 13th channel must be inserted into the correct sorted position among 12 values. With 13 possible insertion positions, a theoretical lower bound is ceil(log2(13)) = 4 comparators. However, sorting networks are oblivious (branchless), and the constraints of merging 1 element into 12 fixed channels require more than 5 comparators. If a sandboxed simulation tests all optimal 12-input prefixes and confirms none allows a 5-comparator merge for the 13th channel, it proves that 44-comparator 13-input networks do not contain a 39-comparator 12-input prefix, strongly constraining the search space.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
